definition: A line, phrase or idea in machine output that was never asked for but proves better than what was; the happy accident kept in the final work.
etymology: From gift (Old Norse gipt) + line; after the woodworker’s habit of following a flaw in the grain. A maker finds a knot or a swirl in the board and, instead of cutting it out, builds the piece around it.
in_use: The whole tagline was a giftline — I asked for ten safe options and kept the accident.
the_case: Not every surprise from a machine is a mistake to catch. It names the one worth keeping, and puts the skill where it belongs: the machine made the line by accident; you knew it when you saw it.
seo_title: giftline: the line you never asked the machine for, and kept
